newsitem.title: USA: Norton says will draft welfare bill for D.C.
newsitem.headline: Norton says will draft welfare bill for D.C.

text.p: Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton said she will draft a special welfare reform bill for the District of Columbia, saying the law recently passed by Congress to reform welfare nationwide would compound the District's financial problems.

Norton, the District's non-voting representative in Congress, wrote to Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala asking the Clinton administration for help in drafting the bill. Norton said the new welfare law, which was signed by President Clinton last month, was "based on a federal-state model that is wholly inapplicable to the District."
"The difference is that other cities have states that will act as safety nets, while the District lacks any state," Norton said.

The new law requires that next year every state and the District put 25 percent of it welfare recipients to work or lose up to 5 percent of its federal welfare funds. Last week, the Clinton administration withdrew its approval of a waiver that would have softened some effects of the bill on the District. Norton argued that the new law leaves the city in a "virtually impossible position -- enforce an unenforceable bill ... or face increasing annual losses of federal funds, guaranteed to compound the District's insolvency."

A spokeswoman for Shalala said the department had received the letter. "All I can really tell you is we plan to provide the District as well as all 50 states the assistance they need to implement the new law," Shalala's spokeswoman, Melissa Skolfield, said.
